newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada, Brazil firms seek value in sugar waste.
newsitem.headline: Canada, Brazil firms seek value in sugar waste.

text.p: DynaMotive Technologies Corp of Canada said on Tuesday it signed a letter of understanding with one of the world's largest sugar producers to form a joint venture in Brazil that would convert sugar refinery waste into fuels and chemicals.
DynaMotive declined to identify the partner but said it was a Brazilian firm that processed seven million tons of sugar cane a year. A DynaMotive spokesman said the company was publicly held.

Under the deal, the two companies will seek to commercialize Dynamotive's BioMass Refinery technology. The system would convert organic waste such as sugar cane leaves and bagasse into solid and liquid fuels, value-added chemicals and fertilizers.

"As one of the key players in a highly competitive commodity market, our Brazilian partner (wants)...to find innovative ways to extract more value from its sugar cane waste streams by integrating DynaMotive's proprietary technologies with its sugar-making process," DynaMotive chief Reinhold Roth said.
DynaMotive said the value of the byproducts could exceed the value of the sugar itself.
The letter of understanding gives the two companies 60 days to conduct due diligence and study market opportunities. No financial details were disclosed.
